title: Dashboards: correlate model version change rate with rollout phases and incident/regression signals
author: Logan Wright
description: Context: As part of the model metadata schema + changelog generator rollout, we now emit structured model change events (promotions, rollbacks, metadata edits) and rollout phase transitions. Support and oncall repeatedly asked for a fast way to answer: “did this latency/regression coincide with a model version promotion or rollout phase change?” This PR adds Grafana panels + recording rules to correlate: (1) model version change rate, (2) rollout phase transitions (canary/A-B/GA/rollback), and (3) incident/regression signals (5xx, timeouts, p95/p99 latency, eval-guardrail failures when present). What’s included: - New dashboard: “Model Rollout Correlation” with panels for change rate over time, rollout phase annotations, and ‘before/after’ latency + error overlays. - Update existing “LLM Serving Overview” dashboard with a compact panel showing model version change rate by deployment_mode and model_name (top 10) plus a click-through to the correlation dashboard. - Prometheus recording rules to normalize and de-cardinalize model change counters for dashboards (avoid high-cardinality labels from raw events). - Standard annotations schema for rollout phase changes (Grafana annotations sourced from Loki logs) to visualize canary/A-B boundaries. Notes/assumptions: - This depends on control-plane emitting model_change and rollout_phase_change events (redwood PR #18435 / #18458). In environments where those logs/metrics aren’t present yet, panels will render ‘No data’ but won’t break dashboards. - We intentionally do not include per-customer/account identifiers in any metric labelset; correlation for account-specific cases should use trace IDs / audit tooling, not dashboards. - Private deployments: these dashboards assume the “control-plane-events” log stream is configured; otherwise skip the annotations panel per docs added here.
commits: Add recording rules for model change event counters (normalized label set)
Add Grafana dashboard: model rollout correlation
Add annotation query templates for rollout phase transitions
Wire model change rate panel into LLM Serving Overview
Docs: troubleshooting + rollout correlation playbook snippet
Chore: dashboard jsonnet formatting + lint fixes
implementation_notes: Metrics inputs: - counter: redwood_control_plane_model_change_events_total{action="promote"|"rollback"|"metadata_update", deployment_mode, model_name, model_version} (raw; high-cardinality due to version) - counter: redwood_control_plane_rollout_phase_events_total{phase, deployment_mode, model_name, rollout_id} (raw; rollout_id high-cardinality) This PR adds recording rules to collapse labels for dashboards: - redwood:model_change_events:rate5m{action, deployment_mode, model_name} = sum without(model_version,region,cluster) (rate(redwood_control_plane_model_change_events_total[5m])) - redwood:rollout_phase_transitions:rate5m{phase, deployment_mode, model_name} = sum without(rollout_id,region,cluster) (rate(redwood_control_plane_rollout_phase_events_total[5m])) Correlation dashboard panels: - “Model version change rate (promote/rollback)” time series, stacked by action - “Rollout phase transition rate” time series (canary/ab/ga) - “Errors & latency overlay” showing requests_error_rate and p95 latency for the same model_name + deployment_mode, with the above series as overlays - “Regression signals” panel: guardrail_fail_rate (if present) and ‘quality_regression_flag’ (0/1) when eval harness emits it (optional) Grafana annotations: - Source: Loki stream {app="control-plane", component="eventing"} | json | event_type in ("rollout_phase_change") - Annotation text includes: model_name, phase, rollout_id (NOT used as a metric label; only shown in the annotation tooltip).
testing: Local: jsonnet render + grafana-dashboard-linter, promtool check rules. Staging: validated dashboard renders against staging metrics (rollouts dogfood environment). Verified panels show ‘No data’ gracefully when model change metrics absent by toggling datasource to a sandbox Prometheus. Verified that label cardinality does not grow with model_version or rollout_id by inspecting series count for redwood:model_change_events:rate5m and redwood:rollout_phase_transitions:rate5m.
screenshots: Screenshot (staging): Model Rollout Correlation dashboard showing a promotion spike aligned with canary->A/B annotation and concurrent p95 increase.
Screenshot (staging): LLM Serving Overview new panel with top model change rates and link-out.
review_conversation: Jada Williams (requested changes): The change-rate panel is useful, but please ensure the recording rules strip model_version; otherwise dashboards will explode in cardinality for frequent promotions. Also can we align naming with the schema doc: ‘promote’ vs ‘promotion’? Logan Wright (author): Good catch. Updated rules to sum without(model_version, rollout_id) and standardized action values to promote/rollback/metadata_update in the rule expression + legend. Michael Nguyen (requested changes): For rollbacks, we should be able to distinguish “auto-fallback” vs “manual rollback” eventually. Not blocking, but can you at least leave a TODO in the dashboard and avoid encoding that as a label now. Logan Wright: Added a dashboard note + TODO in docs; no label added. Leila Farouk (QA): Can you add a snapshot test (jsonnet render diff) to prevent accidental dashboard churn? Logan Wright: Added a CI step that renders jsonnet and checks in the rendered output hash; also tightened formatting so diffs are stable. Dylan Brooks (approve): This unblocks the Console + Support story; thanks. Please link the runbook from the oncall handbook in a follow-up. Logan Wright: Ack; will file a follow-up PR in docs repo.
post_merge_notes: Follow-ups: (1) add oncall handbook link to docs/runbooks/model-rollout-correlation.md, (2) once rollout_phase_change events are fully deployed, switch annotations to the dedicated events index instead of parsing control-plane logs, (3) evaluate adding a lightweight ‘incident overlay’ annotation feed (PagerDuty) for tighter correlation.
